source: Transit axis. The base rule is COMPUTED in build.py (not stored here): transit is 'free' wherever the entry type is visa-free or freedom-of-movement, because airside transit is strictly less privileged than entry — if you can enter a country without a visa, you can always remain in its international transit area. Every other corridor defaults to 'unknown'.
note: Curated, cited rules. 'policies' has two kinds: (a) a list -- one uniform transit value + note over the cross product of a passport set and a destination set (e.g. the Schengen airport-transit-visa lists) -- and (b) a default -- fill every 'unknown' corridor of one or more destinations (optionally limited to certain entry types) with a value, then override 'exempt' passports (e.g. the UK DATV, US C-1 and China TWOV regimes). Both only fill corridors the base rule left 'unknown'; policy order in the array sets precedence over those 'unknown' corridors, and neither overrides a visa-free-entry 'free'. 'overrides' are explicit per-corridor rules, the most specific form, applied last so they always win. Transit values: 'required' = a transit visa is needed even for an airside connection (the high-value safety case); 'free' = no transit visa is needed despite a non-visa-free entry requirement (e.g. the Schengen airside transit privilege); 'conditional' = transit is permitted but only with booked, legally-approved onward travel to a third country (e.g. China 24h / 240h TWOV). Each entry carries source_page + source_url.

policies.name: schengen_atv_core
policies.note: Airport transit visa (ATV) required to transit airside through any Schengen airport (or Cyprus), even without leaving the international transit area (EU common list, Visa Code Reg. 810/2009). Not required if you hold a valid EU/EEA/CA/JP/US visa or residence permit.

policies.name: schengen_transit_privilege
policies.default_note: Airside transit privilege: transiting airside through a Schengen (or Cyprus) airport -- without leaving the international transit area, single airport, under one day -- requires no transit visa for any nationality.

policies.name: uk_datv
policies.default_note: Direct Airside Transit visa (DATV) required to transit airside through the UK -- airside transit is available only at London Heathrow and Manchester -- when you need a visa to enter and are not on the exempt list.
policies.exempt_note: No DATV needed for these nationalities (airside transit at LHR/MAN). Taiwan: non-PIN passports only; Venezuela: biometric passports only. Also exempt if you hold a valid AU/CA/NZ/US visa or an EEA/UK residence permit.
policies.source_page: Visa policy of the United Kingdom

policies.name: us_c1
policies.default_note: C-1 transit visa required to transit through the United States (immediate and continuous transit en route to another country) when you need a visa to enter. VWP (visa-free) nationals do not need a C-1 -- they use ESTA.
policies.source_page: Visa policy of the United States

policies.name: cn_twov
policies.default_note: 24-hour transit without visa (TWOV): transit through mainland China without a visa for up to 24 hours -- arrive by air, cruise ship or rail with a confirmed (not standby) onward ticket to a third country departing within 24 hours; passport valid 3+ months. Available to most nationalities at most ports, especially for airside connections.
policies.exempt_note: 240-hour (10-day) visa-free transit (TWOV): these 57 nationalities may transit through mainland China without a visa for up to 10 days via the 47 designated airports plus sea/rail/land ports, moving within 24 eligible provinces/municipalities, continuing to a third country (arrival and onward destinations must differ); passport valid 3+ months and onward ticket/visa required. China's longest transit exemption.

policies.name: ae_airside
policies.default_note: Airside transit through the UAE requires no transit visa -- you may remain in the international transit area (all travellers are exempt from entry fees for the first 48 hours). A 96-hour transit visa is issued at the airport if you leave the transit area or your layover exceeds 48 hours (hotel booking required for some nationalities). Nationals of Iran are refused entry and transit (2026).
policies.source_page: Visa policy of the United Arab Emirates

policies.name: qa_airside
policies.default_note: Airside transit through Hamad International Airport requires no transit visa regardless of nationality if you depart within 24 hours. Qatar Airways passengers with layovers of 5 to 96 hours can obtain a free transit visa to leave the airport.

policies.name: om_airside
policies.default_note: Airside transit through Oman without a visa for up to 6 hours is allowed for any nationality proceeding by the same flight with an onward ticket.

policies.name: br_airside
policies.default_note: No visa is required for airport transit from any nationality, as long as you do not leave the international transit area.

policies.name: ru_airside
policies.default_note: Airside transit of less than 24 hours requires no visa in most circumstances, provided you hold a confirmed onward ticket and remain in the international transit area without clearing passport control. A number of Russian airports have no international transit area, so a transit visa is required to change planes there.

policies.name: sg_airside
policies.default_note: Airside transit through Changi Airport requires no visa if you hold an onward ticket, remain in the transit area, keep luggage checked to your final destination and do not clear immigration (not available on low-cost carriers other than Scoot-thru and Jetstar). Separately, the 96-hour Visa-Free Transit Facility lets nationals of China and India (and CIS, Georgia, Moldova, Turkmenistan, Ukraine) ENTER Singapore for up to 96 hours when transiting to or from a third country with a qualifying visa.

policies.name: kr_airside
policies.default_note: Airside transit through South Korea requires no visa for less than 24 hours at Incheon (or the same calendar day at other airports), as long as you stay within the transit area. Non-visa-exempt nationals may also qualify for a 30-day transit visa exemption if they hold a visa or residence permit from Australia, Canada and other listed states and meet the routing rules.

policies.name: jp_airside
policies.default_note: Airside transit through Japan requires no visa while you remain in the transit area. The 72-hour transit-without-visa (TWOV) additionally allows entry for up to 72 hours (sightseeing, rest) when you are transiting to a third country and obtain a transit or shore pass from the carrier.

policies.name: tr_airside
policies.default_note: Airside transit privilege: transiting airside through a single Turkish airport, staying in the international transit area and under one day, requires no visa for most nationalities (the transfer must be possible without leaving the transit area). Landside transit always requires a visa for visa nationals; a small number of nationalities still need a transit visa even for airside transit depending on the final destination, and travellers bound for Northern Cyprus need a double airport transit visa.

policies.name: au_transit
policies.default_note: Transit visa (subclass 771) required to transit airside through Australia unless you are on the transit-without-visa list or you depart by air within 8 hours of arrival with a confirmed onward booking and remain in the transit lounge. A Transit visa is always required for Gold Coast airport, and for Cairns and Sydney if staying overnight.
policies.exempt_note: On Australia's transit-without-visa list -- no Transit visa (771) needed for airside connections under the 8-hour rule; an electronic travel declaration (ETA/e600) may still be required to board.

policies.name: ca_transit
policies.default_note: A transit visa is required to transit through Canada when you need a visa or eTA to enter. Narrow exemption: the Transit Without Visa (TWOV) and China Transit Program (CTP) allow certain nationals -- Indonesia, the Philippines, Taiwan and Thailand (TWOV), and Chinese passport holders via CTP -- to transit airside without a transit visa if they hold a valid U.S. visa, use a participating airport (Vancouver, Calgary, Winnipeg, Toronto P.E. Trudeau, or Montreal for CTP), and leave within 24 hours staying in the sterile international transit area.

policies.name: nz_transit
policies.default_note: A Transit Visa is required to transit through New Zealand (airside, Auckland Airport only, up to 24 hours) when you are not a visa-waiver national and are not on the transit visa waiver list.
policies.exempt_note: On New Zealand's transit visa waiver list -- no Transit Visa needed (a transit eTA is required), airside at Auckland Airport only, up to 24 hours.

policies.name: in_transit
policies.default_note: India requires a transit visa (15 days, single or double entry, onward ticket needed) or a transit e-Visa (30 days) to transit through the country; apply before travel. Some short airside connections may be exempt -- verify with your airline or the Bureau of Immigration.

policies.name: au_eta_airside
policies.default_note: Visa-exempt (ETA) nationals can transit airside through Australia without a Transit visa (771); an electronic travel declaration (ETA/e600) may still be required to board.

policies.name: ca_eta_airside
policies.default_note: Visa-exempt (eTA) nationals can transit airside through Canada without a transit visa.

policies.name: nz_eta_airside
policies.default_note: Visa-waiver (nZeTA) nationals can transit airside through New Zealand without a Transit Visa (a transit eTA is required), Auckland Airport only, up to 24 hours.
